title: MoD inks contract with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc for leasing of two MQ-9B Sea Guardian High-Altitude Long-Endurance Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems for Indian Navy for 30 months
body_text:
The Ministry of Defence has signed a contract with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI) for the leasing of two MQ-9B Sea Guardian High-Altitude Long-Endurance (HALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) for the Indian Navy for a period of 30 months. The contract is valued at approximately Rs 1,943 crore. It was signed in the presence of Additional Secretary & Director General (Acquisition), Department of Defence, Shri A. Anbarasu, at Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi on August 17, 2026.
The MQ-9B Sea Guardian HALE RPAS, equipped with advanced systems, state-of-the-art sensors and sophisticated payloads, will significantly enhance the Indian Navy’s Maritime Domain Awareness capabilities. The systems will provide persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance coverage over vast areas of the maritime domain, strengthening India’s ability to monitor and respond to developments across the Indian Ocean Region.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed a Rs 1,943 crore contract with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI) to lease two MQ-9B Sea Guardian High-Altitude Long-Endurance Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) for the Indian Navy for 30 months. The contract was signed on 17 August 2026 in New Delhi in the presence of Additional Secretary & DG (Acquisition) A. Anbarasu. The drones are intended to boost the Navy's Maritime Domain Awareness through persistent ISR coverage over the Indian Ocean Region.
enrichment.context:
The MQ-9B Sea Guardian is the maritime variant of General Atomics' MQ-9B Predator drone family, capable of long-endurance surveillance, anti-submarine warfare support, and intelligence gathering. This lease follows India's landmark 2024 government-to-government deal to procure 31 MQ-9B drones (Sea Guardians for the Navy and Sky Guardians for the Army and Air Force) for approximately $3.99 billion, aimed at strengthening surveillance along India's maritime borders and the broader Indian Ocean Region amid growing Chinese naval activity. Leasing platforms in the interim, as in this contract, allows the Navy to bridge capability gaps in maritime domain awareness while the larger acquisition program is being executed.

Enhanced ISR capability over the Indian Ocean Region is significant given India's strategic interest in monitoring sea lanes of communication, anti-piracy operations, and countering the growing presence of extra-regional naval forces. This contract represents an incremental but concrete step in operationalizing India's broader unmanned systems strategy for maritime security, complementing initiatives like SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and India's expanding blue-water naval posture.

prelims_questions.question: The MQ-9B Sea Guardian, recently leased by India for its Navy, is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
options: High-Altitude Long-Endurance Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release describes the MQ-9B Sea Guardian as a High-Altitude Long-Endurance Remotely Piloted Aircraft System designed to provide persistent ISR coverage over maritime areas, enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness.

prelims_questions.question: The MQ-9B Sea Guardian RPAS leased by the Indian Navy is manufactured by which company?
prelims_questions.explanation: The contract was signed with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), the US-based manufacturer of the MQ-9B Predator/Sea Guardian family of drones.
